setting: the hill at ten past eight on the morning after a third night, his breathing heavy on the descent and his voice flattened out to nearly nothing, a delivery lorry reversing somewhere below, two sentences begun and abandoned before he says only that the ward was full and the corridor was worse, a gate latch, then twelve seconds of walking with no words in it at all

the stripped art room after the last bell, her footsteps echoing in a way they have not all year, a chair being set down on a table mid sentence, a window catch rattling, her voice bright and then dropping when she gets to the bare wall behind the plan chest, a long pause, keys, and the door shutting on the last two seconds

the bottom of the hill on a cool bright morning after the borrowed night, gulls somewhere over the roofs, a paper bag under his arm rustling on every step, the word saturday said twice, once flat and once slower, a list of three things he intends to do before he sleeps of which he only manages to name two

the climb up to his flat at ten to nine at night with salt still on him, slower than his usual walk and stopping twice, a car passing and the sound of his own keys, his voice lower and warmer than it ever is in the morning, one long unfilled gap where he only breathes and the traffic goes past, and the last sentence cut off by the stairwell door

the walk down on the morning of the last night of a run, birds and no traffic yet, his voice thinned right out, a bin lid dropping somewhere behind him, a remark about being thirty two tomorrow made once and immediately talked over with something about bread, footsteps stopping at a crossing and starting again
